title: Early-Career Employment Decline in AI-Exposed Occupations
description: Employment decline for workers aged 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations, measured relative to less-exposed occupations. Only relative or regression-adjusted estimates are plotted; raw unadjusted declines measure a different quantity and appear as overlays.
disclaimer: Every plotted point is a relative estimate — the employment gap between early-career workers in most-exposed versus least-exposed occupations — not an absolute headcount drop. Aggregate employment in exposed occupations has continued to grow across all ages; this effect is specific to the 22-25 cohort. Non-US estimates (Sweden, Netherlands) are shown as overlays because geography is a hard gate on comparability. One caveat about mechanism: these are exposure-based estimates, and exposure may capture what employers expect AI to do rather than what it already does. Only about 5.9% of eligible hiring firms show measurable AI adoption, and firms that have adopted are growing headcount faster than those that have not — so the early-career gap is unlikely to be driven mainly by AI already performing these jobs. Hiring appears to pull back in occupations where employers anticipate AI becoming capable. See [Revelio Labs](https://www.reveliolabs.com/news/ai-and-work/introduction-the-revelio-ai-labor-market-tracker) and [Known Limitations](/methodology#limitations).

overlays.label: Stanford/ADP: raw employment for ages 22-25 in exposed jobs fell 6%

sources.title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of AI
sources.publisher: Stanford Digital Economy Lab (Brynjolfsson, Chandar, Chen)
sources.excerpt: Early-career workers (ages 22-25) in the most AI-exposed occupations have experienced a 16 percent relative decline in employment even after controlling for firm-level shocks. By September 2025, employment for software developers aged 22-25 declined nearly 20% compared to its peak in late 2022.

sources.title: Young workers' employment drops in occupations with high AI exposure
sources.excerpt: Workers age 22-25 in most AI-exposed occupations experienced 13% employment decline since 2022, driven by fewer workforce entrants rather than higher separations. Employment share for AI-exposed occupations fell from 16.4% (Nov 2022) to 15.5% (Sep 2025).

sources.title: AI and Coder Employment: Compiling the Evidence
sources.excerpt: They find that among 22-25 year olds employment in the top two quartiles of AI exposure fell about 12 percent relative to employment in the bottom quartile.

sources.title: You're (not) hired: Artificial intelligence and early career hiring in the Quarterly Workforce Indicators
sources.excerpt: Regression-adjusted employment of early career workers in the most AI-exposed quintile of industry-state cells declined by 12% over the 10 quarters following the introduction of ChatGPT, even as employment in less-exposed industries rose.

sources.title: Yes, AI Is Affecting Employment. Here's the Data
sources.excerpt: In jobs with high AI exposure, employment for 22- to 25-year-olds fell 6% between late 2022 and July 2025. Software developers saw a 20% early-career decline. Employment among workers 30 and older grew 6-13%.

sources.title: Looking for the Ladder: Is AI Impacting Entry-Level Jobs?
sources.excerpt: Entry-level hiring rates have declined 23 percent compared to pre-pandemic levels, a steeper drop than the 18 percent decline for overall hiring.

sources.title: Dalende werkgelegenheid onder Nederlandse jongeren die concurreren met GenAI
sources.excerpt: In het derde kwartaal van 2025 werkten ruim dertien procent minder jongeren in de meest vatbare beroepsgroepen dan in het vierde kwartaal van 2022, terwijl de werkgelegenheid in andere beroepsgroepen juist drie procent steeg.

sources.title: Same Storm, Different Boats: Generative AI and the Age Gradient in Hiring
sources.publisher: RATIO Institute / Örebro University (Lodefalk, Löthman, Koch, Engberg)
sources.excerpt: An event study documents an accelerating decline in employment of 22-25-year-olds in high-AI-exposure occupations, reaching 5.5 per cent by early 2025 relative to less exposed occupations within the same employers.

sources.title: What We Do and Don't Know About How AI is Affecting the Labor Market
sources.publisher: The Budget Lab at Yale (Gimbel, Kendall, Nunn)
sources.excerpt: We therefore investigated effects for workers 34 and younger, finding mixed evidence of AI effects for this group... roughly half a percentage point increase in the entire sample, and more for the 16-34 year old subsample - but both statistically insignificant.

sources.title: I'm the C.E.O. of Goldman Sachs. The A.I. Job Apocalypse Is Overblown.
sources.publisher: The New York Times (David M. Solomon, CEO Goldman Sachs)
sources.excerpt: According to one Stanford study, in the occupations most susceptible to greater automation, such as software engineering or customer service, entry-level employment has already declined by 16 percent relative to the least-exposed occupations.

sources.title: Stanford DEL Canaries Dashboard: July 2026 Update
sources.publisher: Stanford Digital Economy Lab / ADP Research
sources.excerpt: In the most-exposed quintile, employment among early-career women has been contracting at 4.5% per year since the introduction of ChatGPT in November 2022, while employment for men of the same age is contracting at 2.5% per year.

sources.title: AI Labor Market Tracker: July 2026
sources.excerpt: Employment for younger workers in the most AI-exposed occupations is down by 13% relative to the least exposed occupations, since pre-ChatGPT — a much larger decline than for older workers. Event-study with two-way occupation and month fixed effects, standard errors clustered by occupation, ages 22-25, built on online professional profiles rather than payroll records.
